prompts.title: Recent Form: Wins, Draws, Losses
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 motion-graphics scene, six to ten seconds, for a narration line about recent form. Editorial variant first: kinetic typography with Spanish team names Lech Poznań and Sunderland; no statistical axes, no sample claims and no invented match events. Composition: warm-white team names enter as large slabs from opposite edges and snap into a stacked lockup in the upper half; a lime rhythmic bar pulses under each name on the beat; charcoal #101412 background, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf; condensed sans typography; one focal point on the team lockup; lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles, with all labels kept above that band. Entry 0.0–1.2 s: names slide in with a hard ease-out; 1.2–4.5 s: rhythmic emphasis alternates between the names as the narration names each side; 4.5–6.0 s: a slate seam wipes across and the names exit upward. Camera: slow lateral drift with a slight push-in; transition: lime wipe; exit: cut to statistical block. Statistical variant: grouped count bars, one group per team, with bars for wins, draws and losses; x-axis Spanish labels Victorias, Empates and Derrotas; y-axis unit partidos; all bars share one common count scale and a shared zero baseline computed from the facts. Values are {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}} for Lech Poznań and {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}} for Sunderland. Sample annotation above the subtitle band prints {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} with the Spanish label Muestra; if the values differ, a small slate flag marks the unequal samples. Source tag: Bzzoiro, lastMatches sample. Entry 0.0–1.0 s: zero line draws; 1.0–3.0 s: bars grow in a staggered beat; 3.0–5.5 s: main comparison holds, with the wins bar getting lime emphasis; 5.5–7.0 s: source and sample annotation fade in; camera is locked with a micro push; transition is a slate dissolve; exit is a quick cut. Maintain professional hierarchy, legible Spanish labels and one focal point on the win-count contrast.

prompts.title: Goals For and Against
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16, six to ten seconds, goals context. Editorial variant: illustrative football pitch on charcoal #101412, drawn in slate #8ca6bf lines with warm-white markings; team names in Spanish, Lech Poznań and Sunderland, sit in the upper half; a lime #c5ed74 ball path arcs from a defensive third to an attacking third as an abstract motif, not a replay or invented match event; no statistical axes and no sample claims. Typography is condensed sans in warm white, with one focal point on the ball path and the two-name lockup. Lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles; keep pitch labels above that band. Entry 0.0–1.2 s: pitch lines draw in perspective; 1.2–3.5 s: names slide in from left and right; 3.5–6.0 s: ball trail sweeps once, pauses, then names compress toward the centre; 6.0–8.0 s: exit via a slate curtain wipe; camera: slow overhead push with parallax; transition: lime streak; exit: hard cut. Statistical variant: paired horizontal bars for goals for and goals against, one pair per team, same goals unit and one common goals scale with a zero baseline; Spanish labels Goles a favor and Goles recibidos; team labels Lech Poznań and Sunderland. Values are {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}} for the home pair, {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}} for the away pair. Sample annotation reads Muestra {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} and sits above the subtitle band; source tag: Bzzoiro, lastMatches sample. Entry 0.0–1.0 s: axis and zero line draw; 1.0–3.2 s: bars extend from zero in paired rhythm; 3.2–5.5 s: main comparison holds, goals-for bars take lime emphasis; 5.5–7.0 s: source and sample annotation fade in; camera locked with subtle vertical drift; transition: warm-white flash frame; exit: bars collapse to zero. Keep professional hierarchy, legible Spanish labels and one focal point on the goals-for versus goals-against pairing.

prompts.title: Clean Sheets vs Sample Size
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16, six to ten seconds, clean-sheets comparison. Editorial variant: stylised shield as the hero shape, defensive energy expressed by a slow lime #c5ed74 charge moving across a charcoal #101412 field; warm-white team names in Spanish, Lech Poznań and Sunderland, are set on opposite sides of the shield; slate #8ca6bf ribs and a subtle pulse suggest resistance without showing invented match events; no statistical axes, no sample claims. Typography is bold condensed; one focal point is the shield core; lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles, all labels above it. Entry 0.0–1.2 s: shield edges draw; 1.2–3.5 s: team names lock in; 3.5–6.0 s: lime energy rings expand once and settle; 6.0–8.0 s: shield splits and exits as a slate wipe; camera: slow push-in with slight tilt; transition: shield-edge wipe; exit: cut. Statistical variant: count bars for clean sheets, one bar per team, unit partidos, shared zero baseline and one common count scale; do not convert counts into rates. Spanish labels Arcos en cero and Muestra; values are {{home.clean}} for Lech Poznań and {{away.clean}} for Sunderland. Sample annotation prints {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} separately so counts and sample sizes stay distinct; source tag: Bzzoiro, lastMatches sample. Entry 0.0–1.0 s: zero line draws; 1.0–3.0 s: bars rise; 3.0–5.5 s: main comparison holds, with the larger count taking lime emphasis only by fact value; 5.5–7.0 s: source and sample annotation fade in; camera locked; transition: slate dissolve; exit: bars shrink to zero. Maintain professional hierarchy, legible Spanish labels and one focal point on the clean-sheet count contrast.

prompts.title: Synthesis: Wins and Clean Sheets
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16, six to ten seconds, synthesis of one grounded statistical tension built from compatible available facts: recent win count against clean-sheet count, with no prediction. Editorial variant first: team reveals with narrative emphasis; no statistical axes, no sample claims and no invented match events. Composition: two charcoal #101412 slabs slide in from opposite edges, warm-white Spanish team names Lech Poznań and Sunderland stamped on each; a central seam of slate #8ca6bf holds them apart; a lime #c5ed74 pulse travels along the seam as the tension marker; condensed sans typography; one focal point on the seam and the two names; lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles, labels above that band. Entry 0.0–1.2 s: slabs enter; 1.2–3.8 s: names reveal in sequence; 3.8–6.0 s: lime pulse crosses once and the slabs press toward the seam; 6.0–8.0 s: exit via a vertical slate wipe; camera: slow push-in with parallax; transition: seam split; exit: cut to statistical block. Statistical variant: two paired mini count-bar charts, one for Victorias and one for Arcos en cero, both unit partidos; each mini chart has a shared zero baseline and a common count scale across the two teams, and the metrics are not plotted against each other. Values are {{home.wins}} and {{away.wins}} for Victorias, {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}} for Arcos en cero. Spanish labels and source-attributed annotations read Historial reciente and Muestra {{home.n}} and {{away.n}}; source tag: Bzzoiro, lastMatches sample. No model estimate is shown because none is published, and the scene makes no predictive claim. Entry 0.0–1.0 s: both zero lines draw; 1.0–3.2 s: bars grow; 3.2–5.5 s: main comparison holds, with the two count gaps getting lime emphasis; 5.5–7.0 s: source and sample annotation fade in; camera locked with micro push; transition: slate dissolve; exit: quick cut. Keep professional hierarchy, legible Spanish labels and one focal point on the wins-versus-clean-sheets tension.
